notes.decision: Translated 'continent one' (ἐγκρατής) preserving the Greek loanword's ascetic-philosophical sense. The text develops a multi-register exegesis: the same title applies (1) to the captive Light that mingled and was extracted, (2) to the metangismos remainder, (3) to the New Man, (4) to the celibate man, (5) to the once-married man who later renounces. Each register is a distinct correspondential application of the same name.

Retained as 'virgin' (Greek παρθένος) — both the cosmic Light-icon chosen in the Ambassador (l.7-9), the Mind of Light who bears the icons of the elect (l.16-17), and the celibate human (l.21-22) bear this title. The text is enumerating different cosmological registers of one name.

Greek μετάγγισμός 'transfusion, transmutation' — Manichaean technical term for the cosmic transmigration / trans-pouring of light substance from vessel to vessel. Translated 'transmutation' to preserve the technical sense; the chapter title at line 32 confirms this is the topic to be expounded next.
Translated 'New Man' per accumulated glossary (ⲡⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ = Pauline καινὸς ἄνθρωπος). Antithetical pair-partner ⲡⲓⲣⲙ̄ⲛⲉⲥ 'the Old Man' on the same line confirms the Pauline anthropological register.

Read as ⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ = ⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ 'wife' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ). The initial ⲑⲩ- is unusual — possibly a scribal artifact or Lyc. orthographic feature of the indefinite-article cluster ⲟⲩ-. Context (the man who has X in the world, then later purifies himself from her) decisively requires 'wife.'

Six-character lacuna preserving partial ϥ̄ (3sg.m). Reading the syntactic frame ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ⲡⲉⲓ ⲁⲉ ϥ̄[verb] ⲛϩⲣ̄ ⲟⲩⲉⲅⲕⲣⲁⲧⲏⲥ '...he {verb}s and becomes a continent one,' the missing material likely contained a verb such as ϥ̄ⲛⲁⲣ̄ 'he shall become' or ϥ̄ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'he becomes.' Left as lacuna because surface traces are insufficient to fix the reading.

Chapter-end colophon: a single ⲯⲑ '99' standing alone marks the boundary closure of the previous chapter (chapter 98 on the senses of virgin/continent), before the new chapter heading at line 32 introduces chapter 99 on transmutation.
Chapter heading framed by chapter number on both sides — standard Manichaean Kephalaia chapter-display convention. Chapter 99 'Concerning the Transmutation/Transmigration.'
